raw.details:
Overview:

CodeBreaker is an online hackathon conducted by Kira’s Logic × CodeBlooded, designed to challenge participants to think creatively, solve real-world problems, and turn their ideas into working prototypes.

Hackathon Format:

The hackathon will be conducted in 3 rounds:

Round 1 — Idea/PPT Submission:

Participants will submit their solution idea in the prescribed PPT format. Submissions will be evaluated based on problem understanding, innovation, feasibility, proposed solution, and overall presentation.

Round 2 — Online Mentorship & Refinement:

Shortlisted teams will receive online mentorship to refine their ideas, improve their technical approach, and develop their prototype. Mentors may provide guidance on technology, implementation, scalability, and presentation.

Round 3 — Grand Finale: Prototype Demonstration:

Finalist teams will present and demonstrate their working prototype online before the judging panel. Teams will explain their solution, demonstrate its functionality, and answer questions from the judges.

Eligibility:

  • Open to students and aspiring developers/innovators.
  • Participants may register individually or as a team.
  • Inter-college teams are allowed.
  • Participants from different academic specializations are allowed.
  • Teams should follow the maximum team-size requirement specified during registration.

Rules:

  • All submissions must be the original work of the participating team.
  • Teams must submit their work within the announced deadlines.
  • Participants may use open-source technologies, APIs, frameworks, and publicly available resources, while complying with their respective licenses.
  • Plagiarism or submission of substantially copied projects may result in disqualification.
  • Teams must be available for the online mentorship and Grand Finale rounds if shortlisted.
  • The prototype demonstrated in the Grand Finale should correspond to the solution submitted during the hackathon.
  • Judges' decisions regarding qualification and evaluation will be final.

Evaluation Criteria:

Projects may be evaluated on:

  • Innovation & Creativity
  • Problem Understanding
  • Technical Implementation
  • Feasibility & Scalability
  • Prototype Functionality
  • Impact & Usefulness
  • Presentation & Demonstration

Mode:

The entire hackathon will be conducted online, including submissions, mentorship sessions, and the Grand Finale prototype demonstration.

Build your idea. Break the problem. Create the solution.
